native_result.query: How were the phases of the Middle Neolithic (3400-3000 BCE) and Younger Neolithic (2900-2300 BCE) characterized in terms of the first principal component in a PCA on the forms of capital analyzed in hundred-year time slices?
native_result.HypoA: During the Middle Neolithic (3400-3000 BCE) and Younger Neolithic (2900-2300 BCE), both phases are primarily associated with negative values on the first principal component (PC1). This Principal component analysis (PCA) is on the forms of capital. The values of the individual elements of the forms of capital form the attributes.
native_result.HypoB: Across the full sequence (4300-500 BCE), PC1 of the 12 capital-form Z variables is a general capital-accumulation axis (positive loadings on copper/gold, hoards, hatchets-swords, daggers, monument count/size, house size and pottery decoration; negative on pottery form, axes-celts, amber, sickle) that rises steadily from the Neolithic into the Bronze Age. Both the Middle Neolithic (3400-3000 BCE) and the Younger Neolithic (2900-2300 BCE, data-table group SG; name mapping given by the task) sit on the negative, low end of this axis: MN starts relatively higher (PC1 about -0.6 at 3400 BCE) and drifts lower (about -1.8 by 3000 BCE), while the Younger Neolithic shows no trend, fluctuating around a low level with event-like spikes at 2700 BCE (monument count, Z=3.95) and 2300 BCE (daggers jumping from -0.58 to +0.80). Refitting the PCA on only the 12 MN+SG slices (sensitivity check; PC1 explains 43.4%) recasts PC1 as domestic/expressive capital (amber, pottery form and decoration, hoards, house size) versus prestige weapons and monument counts; on this axis the Middle Neolithic is consistently high and the Younger Neolithic drops sharply across the 2900-2800 BCE transition (about 3 SD) and stays low. Hypothesis: the two Neolithic phases are characterized not by capital accumulation but by a reorganization of capital - from a household/settlement- and expression-centred portfolio in the Middle Neolithic to a contracted, fluctuating portfolio punctuated by monument- and weapon-related prestige projects in the Younger Neolithic - with overall capital levels in both phases far below the later Bronze Age, against an only marginally changed, still open landscape (pollen openness -0.48 vs -0.57).
native_result.WorkflowB: Loaded capital.csv (39 century slices, comma decimals); verified identity with time_series_data.csv century-mark Z values; correlation-matrix PCA (numpy SVD) on the 12 Z variables with sign fixed so PC1 correlates positively (+0.53) with the composite mean of standardized variables; Fit A on all 39 slices (primary), Fit B on the 12 MN+SG slices only (sensitivity); extracted PC1 scores for MN (3400-3000 BCE, group MN, 5 slices) and YN/SG (2900-2300 BCE, group SG, 7 slices); reported loadings, per-slice score trajectories, stepwise changes and within-period ranges; pollen openness used only as background context.
